page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-4800s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 12 physical cores with 2 threads per core, 192.0 GB of system memory providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and 4800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the CPU features an L1d cache of 32 KB, L2 cache of 0.5 MB, and L3 cache of 16 MB, alongside support for AVX, AES, and SHA-NI instruction sets. The server also includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong processing capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU performance ranking in the top 25%. Passmark CPU tests further confirm this, with the overall CPU score and physics test also placing in the top 25%. In terms of memory performance, the server achieves top-tier status in the top 10% for large-block read-only and write memory bandwidth, though small-block cached read bandwidth and general Passmark memory scores remain in the average tier. Other operations, such as Redis SET performance at 55.54 million operations per second and static web serving throughput at 18.9 GB/sec, fall within the average range.

Given its high resource density, particularly the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and substantial 4800 GB local NVMe SSD storage, this server offers a balanced qualitative cost-efficiency profile for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance without resource contention. This configuration is well-suited for hosting large databases, executing memory-intensive data processing, running software compilation tasks, and managing medium-scale web serving applications.
